title: Worldwide specialist shops — balanced strict-gate production research
status: Imported into data/spots.json as 49 retained machine-draft rows with quality flag d; all remain pending human editorial review and promotion. Mélodies Graphiques was removed after the independent current-status audit.

import.warning: The research evidence remains useful, but catalogue presence does not mean editorial approval. Do not re-import these rows.

method.editorial_contract: A currently trading, independently visitable physical shop whose deep narrow inventory or living trade is itself worth a walking detour.
method.category_rule: Existing Map-2 categories win for books, records, food, bakeries and wine; specialistshops is reserved for otherwise-unrepresented trades and collections.
method.exclusions: Chains, malls, department stores, ordinary antiques, appointment-only dealers, museum shops, design-led concept stores and businesses without a verifiable current storefront.
method.source_policy: At least two useful sources per row, led by a current first-party shop/contact page and supported by a first-party history page or authoritative current listing.
method.coordinate_policy: Named OpenStreetMap feature or exact-address point, checked against the current first-party address.
method.dedupe_policy: Normalized names and aliases checked globally against 16,917 live spots. A 120 m proximity flag triggers manual identity/address review rather than automatic rejection in dense shopping streets.
method.editorial_gate: At least 19/25 overall, with story and walkability each at least 4/5; no padding to reach the target.
method.import_policy: All rows remain draft-only and must receive quality flag d. Current hours or access should be rechecked before publication or travel.

validation.post_import_current_status_audit: 49 retained all-high rows; Mélodies Graphiques deferred because current physical retail and public access could not be proved.

included.q: Dusty Strings harps dulcimers Seattle store
included.w: Harps and hammered dulcimers give this Fremont music shop its unusual centre of gravity. Dusty Strings began in 1979 and still builds those instruments locally; the physical store adds acoustic instruments, lessons and the chance to hear a niche craft rather than merely see it.
_facts: The company began in 1979.
It makes harps and hammered dulcimers and operates a current public Fremont store.

included.s: Eight hundred kinds of washi in Mile End
included.q: Au Papier Japonais washi Montreal
included.w: Roughly 800 kinds of Japanese paper compress into this Mile End shop: translucent, fibrous, patterned and strong enough for conservation or lamps. Tools and small objects explain what the sheets can become, but the real pleasure is learning how many kinds of paper there are.
_facts: The shop carries roughly 800 types of Japanese paper.

included.s: A map shop where the whole world still comes folded
included.q: Metsker Maps First Avenue Seattle
included.w: Wall maps, raised-relief landscapes, globes and folded sheets make navigation physical again at the edge of Pike Place Market. Metsker is an employee-owned single shop, and its staff can still send a walker to the right drawer for an obscure trail or country.
_facts: The current business is employee-owned and operates one downtown Seattle shop.
Its inventory specialises in maps, globes, travel guides and geographic tools.

included.s: A century of obscure kitchen tools in the Italian Market
included.q: Fantes Kitchen Shop Italian Market Philadelphia
included.w: Fante's has served cooks in Philadelphia's Italian Market since 1906. Thousands of practical tools—pasta cutters, pizzelle irons, canning gear, knife parts and moulds for jobs you did not know had a tool—turn an ordinary kitchen shop into a taxonomy of making food.
_facts: The family-owned shop has operated in the Italian Market since 1906.
The physical store carries thousands of professional and home-cooking tools.

included.s: Handmade umbrellas downstairs, their free museum upstairs
included.q: Mario Talarico umbrellas museum Via Toledo Naples
included.w: The Talarico family has made umbrellas in Naples since 1860, shaping handles and repairing its own work rather than treating rainwear as disposable. In May 2026 it opened a free permanent umbrella museum directly above the Via Toledo shop, adding family tools and famous commissions to the detour.
_facts: The family umbrella workshop dates to 1860 and still makes and repairs umbrellas.
A free permanent umbrella museum opened above the shop in May 2026.

included.s: Six generations of marbled paper and Florentine bookbinding
included.q: Giulio Giannini e Figlio marbled paper Florence
included.w: Hand-marbled sheets dry beside albums and books bound in the Florentine style at a workshop founded in 1856. The sixth generation now works from a small lane beside Piazza Pitti, keeping historic blocks, patterns and paper techniques in active use.
_facts: The artistic bookbinding workshop was founded in 1856 and has reached its sixth generation.
It hand-marbles and block-prints paper and maintains a current public shop at Via dei Velluti 1r.
